title: Correction re-queues the row into a cadence dead-end: the sweep re-sends the step message every 15-minute tick forever and the row never advances or terminalizes
detail: correct_reference_call.sql sets status='queued' and next_attempt_at=now() but leaves attempt_count untouched (1 after a T0 bounce, 2/3 after a reminder bounce). sweep_due_reference_calls.sql selects queued rows (status IN ('queued','contact_initiated'), next_attempt_at <= now, taken_over_at IS NULL), so the corrected row is due immediately. process_row (sweep.gleam:280-293) dispatches on attempt_count: 1 -> step_co_nudge (sends the co-nudge EMAIL TO THE APPLICANT, sweep.gleam step_co_nudge -> send.send_co_nudge(to_email: row.applicant_email)), 2/3 -> step_reminder (sends the reminder to the referee). But the claim/advance guards require 'contact_initiated' (sweep_advance.sql:23, sweep_claim_t0.sql:30 requires attempt_count=0), and the corrected row is 'queued' — so the advance 0-rows, the send is NOT rolled back (send-then-claim), next_attempt_at never moves, and the row is re-selected on every tick: the applicant (attempt_count=1) or the corrected referee (2/3) receives the same email every ~15 minutes indefinitely, while the row never reaches reminder-2/terminal. The SQL docstring's contract ('status -> queued, next_attempt_at -> now() so the cadence sweep owns the fresh invite') is not met: no fresh invite is ever sent to the corrected referee (attempt_count=1 rows get only applicant co-nudges), and the corrected row's retained form_token renders 'not found' (classify(queued)=Unknown in form_handler.gleam) if the referee clicks the link the reminder emails carry. The only exit is the landlord taking over (clears next_attempt_at) — the guarded UPDATE stand-down is a 'StoodDown' loop, not a fix. Verified against sweep.gleam process_row/step_co_nudge/step_reminder, sweep_advance.sql, sweep_claim_t0.sql, sweep_due_reference_calls.sql; no sweep test covers a queued row with attempt_count>=1.
evidence: correct_reference_call.sql:16 SET status='queued' (+ attempt_count untouched); sweep_advance.sql:23 AND status='contact_initiated'; sweep_claim_t0.sql:30 AND status='queued' AND attempt_count=0; sweep.gleam:281 attempt_count 1 -> step_co_nudge sends to row.applicant_email; sweep.gleam step_co_nudge sends before sql.sweep_advance (0-row -> StoodDown, next_attempt_at unchanged)

title: Exhaustion fires on delivery failures that never targeted the corrected contact, stamping referee_contact_invalid on an untested corrected channel
detail: The exhaustion gate is `correction_cycles >= 1` + status IN ('queued','contact_initiated') — it never correlates the failed send with the corrected channel. find_reference_call_by_send_ref.sql resolves ANY failure event whose provider id appears anywhere in the row's attempts jsonb (`attempts @> send_ref_json`) or whose recipient equals the effective contact. Two reachable cases: (a) the applicant co-nudge email (sent to the APPLICANT at attempt_count=1, e.g. after a T0-bounce correction) is appended to the row's attempts as a 'delivered' entry with the Resend id (send.gleam email_outcome), so a bounce of that applicant-facing send resolves to the row and — cycles now >= 1 — exhaust_row terminalizes the corrected referee row as unreachable and stamps referee_contact_invalid, even though the corrected referee contact was never attempted; (b) a duplicate/late failure event for the PRE-correction send (e.g. an svix retry or a second event for the same send) arriving after the landlord corrected 0-rowed the awaiting_correction idempotency but now matches the re-queued row and exhausts it. The exhaust_reference_call.sql guard (status IN queued/contact_initiated) happily matches the freshly corrected queued row. This contradicts exhaust_reference_call.sql's own doc ('the signal is never fabricated') — the stamp is derived from the old channel's failure.
evidence: webhooks.gleam:285 `case row.correction_cycles >= 1 { True -> exhaust_row(...)`; find_reference_call_by_send_ref.sql WHERE attempts @> NULLIF($1,'')::jsonb OR effective-contact match; send.gleam:203 email_outcome Ok -> ChannelOutcome(Email, Delivered, email_id) (co-nudge id lands in row.attempts via sweep.gleam step_co_nudge outcomes_to_json); exhaust_reference_call.sql WHERE status IN ('queued','contact_initiated')

title: Clearing one channel in the correction silently reverts to the failed snapshot contact (NULLIF '' -> NULL, then corrected ?? snapshot fallback)
detail: validate_trio (actions_handler.gleam) permits email='' when phone is present. correct_reference_call.sql writes corrected_email = NULLIF($4,'') -> NULL. The sweep's effective_email/effective_phone (sweep.gleam:706-721) fall back to the SNAPSHOT when corrected_* is NULL — so a landlord who clears the address that just bounced (relying on the phone) leaves the failed email live as the effective channel: the next send goes to the same bad address, re-contacting details the system just learned are wrong, violating UX §8.3's 'Never re-contact the same details' rule. The correction cannot express 'no email' — cleared == absent == snapshot. The corrected values are also NOT NULL-free in the panel (corrected_email COALESCE'd '' -> None on the detail read), so the UI cannot distinguish 'cleared' from 'never corrected'.
evidence: correct_reference_call.sql:18 corrected_email = NULLIF($4,''); sweep.gleam:706-712 effective_email `case row.corrected_email { Some(e) -> Some(e); None -> row.contact_email }`; actions_handler.gleam validate_trio allows (name, '', phone)

title: Sweep claim/advance guards lack a taken_over_at re-check: a take-over landing between the due-SELECT and the send does not stop the send
detail: take_over_reference_call.sql documents 'the sweep stops sending — its SELECT already filters taken_over_at IS NULL', but that filter is selection-time only. The sweep is send-then-claim: a take-over committed after the due-SELECT but before/during the send (the send is 1-2 HTTP calls to Resend/Twilio) does not stop the invite/reminder from going out, and the claim still SUCCEEDS because sweep_claim_t0's guard (status='queued' AND attempt_count=0) and sweep_advance's guard (status='contact_initiated' AND attempt_count=$4) are both unaffected by the take-over (which writes only taken_over_at + next_attempt_at). The referee receives a fresh invitation after the landlord took the check over manually (A7 'automated contact ceases' violated in the race window); the row additionally flips to contact_initiated with a minted token. Harmless-but-noisy in most cases; the claim could simply include `AND taken_over_at IS NULL`.
evidence: sweep.gleam step_t0: send.send_invite(...) then sql.sweep_claim_t0(...); sweep_claim_t0.sql:30 AND status='queued' AND attempt_count=0 (no taken_over_at clause); sweep_advance.sql:23-24 (no taken_over_at clause); take_over_reference_call.sql SET taken_over_at=now(), next_attempt_at=NULL, never status

title: Concurrent substitute double-submit can return 409 instead of the documented 200 idempotent no-op
detail: Sequential double-submit is correctly idempotent (the second request's 'existing' SELECT sees the committed successor). But the whole CTE is one statement under READ COMMITTED: if the second request's statement snapshot was taken before the first request committed, the ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING waits for the first transaction, skips the insert, and then the 'existing' SELECT still reads the statement-start snapshot — the committed successor is invisible — 0 rows -> NotSubstitutable -> branded 409 'That reference can't be substituted right now.' A true double-click (two requests in flight within ~tens of ms) can hit this. No duplicate row and no duplicate audit (the invariants hold), but the AD-16 double-submit contract ('must return the existing successor, 200') fails in the race window and the landlord sees a conflict toast after an action that actually succeeded.
evidence: substitute_reference_call.sql: WITH guard/inserted CTE, `SELECT rc.id, 'existing' ... AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inserted)`; actions_handler.gleam do_substitute Ok(Row 0) -> Error(NotSubstitutable) -> 409

title: URL vacancy_id is not validated against the application; a mismatched (landlord-owned) vid silently skips the application-trio update while the action still returns 200
detail: run_action_with_prechecks falls through to action() on verify_vacancy_active returning 0 rows or a query error (only the archived case is rejected), and the vacancy_id is never cross-checked against the application's vacancy. do_correct/do_substitute then run: correct_reference_call / substitute_reference_call succeed (they only scope on call_id + application_id), but update_trio's UPDATE ... WHERE id=$1 AND vacancy_id=$2 0-rows, which the handler treats as success (Ok(_) -> audit + 200). Result: the row is corrected/substituted and the audit written, but the application-level trio (the Off-state chips + the trigger's slot-selection input) keeps the pre-correction contact; a later trigger start on that slot recreates the bad contact. Also silently accepts a wrong vid for take-over (vacancy_uuid unused in do_take_over). Legit SPA traffic always sends the correct vid; reachable only via a crafted/stale URL, hence low.
evidence: actions_handler.gleam:553 `_ -> action()` in the verify_vacancy_active case; update_trio -> sql.update_application_referee_trio_* WHERE id = $1 AND vacancy_id = $2; do_correct `Ok(_) -> audit` ignores the trio row count
